# DropSpace v0.3.0-beta.32

<!-- update-summary: Harden island window lifetimes and async actions, update the Windows runtime, and improve redacted crash diagnostics. -->

## Changes

- Upgrade Windows App SDK to 2.5.1 and refresh the locked dependency graph.
- Retire island surfaces before native cleanup, guard closed/disposed windows, and avoid using retired surfaces while monitors are being rebuilt.
- Recheck window lifetime after asynchronous settings, clipboard, compact-mode and quick-action work. Late completions no longer open dialogs against an already closed island.
- Include HRESULT and redacted exception stack details in error diagnostics to make subsequent crash reports more actionable.
- Explicitly close disconnected native backdrop links on their owning XAML thread, preventing a reproducible hidden-window/garbage-collection fail-fast during finalization.
- Keep one backdrop instance per surface while switching Acrylic controllers, and skip window reconstruction when monitor descriptors have not changed.
- Defer OLE probe cleanup until native drag callbacks unwind, including nested message dispatch.
- Refresh the evergreen bilingual website composition, responsive product showcases and branded navigation without changing release API contracts.
- Add regression coverage for native window lifetime handling and exception-log credential redaction.

## Compatibility and limits

Beta 31 is the immediate upgrade baseline. App identity, data directories and Stable/Beta update channels remain unchanged.

A hidden-window backdrop/GC regression reproduced native 0xc0000409. Matching Microsoft symbols place the original reported fault and the reproduction at the same CloseHelper fail-fast instruction across runtime versions; isolated address evidence identifies native backdrop-link destruction on a non-UI thread. Closing the disconnected link on the XAML thread passes the previously failing regression and both localized lifecycle suites. The original user-process dump was unavailable, so its exact external trigger remains unobserved. This does not claim to eliminate every crash.

Publication requires the exact release commit's Windows tests, WinUI build, installer and portable lifecycle checks, packaging and release validation. Automated coverage does not replace physical mixed-DPI and real-player testing.
